To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following processes are the most important for urban land surface models: multiple reflections of solar radiation, reduction of the sky view factor, surface temperature contrast, and vegetation evaporation.

the urban heat island effect is a result of the following physical processes: (1) multiple reflections of solar radiation within the street canyon, which leads to an increase in the amount of shortwave radiation absorbed by the canyon surfaces; (2) the contrast in the surface temperatures of the canyon surfaces; and (3) the contrast in albedo of the canyon surfaces, which leads to a reduction in the amount and a change in the spectral distribution of longwave radiation emitted from the sky.

the urban surface– atmosphere interactions are dominated by the multiple reflections within street cany ons, the reduction of the visible sky, the contrast in surface temperature, and the evaporation from the vegetation.
